title: Do afternoon naps make you more productive or wreck the rest of your day?
text:
A 19-year study out this month linked long, frequent and morning naps in older adults to declining health. It's about people in their 50s and up, and it's an association, so it says more about naps as a warning sign than about naps being bad. But it got me thinking about how mixed my own experience has been.

A 15 to 20 minute nap after lunch, before 3 PM, used to save my afternoons when I was in corporate. Anything past 30 minutes and I'd wake up groggy, lose the next hour, and then struggle to fall asleep at night.

For people who nap on workdays: how long, what time, and do you use an alarm or caffeine before it? And for those who stopped napping, what replaced it?

(Disclosure: I run a small supplement company, so weigh my take accordingly. No products or links in this post.)
